mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and HOUST drops by more than 10% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins expand in cyclical sectors.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 3% for four consecutive months signals a sustained weakening in consumer demand, which depresses corporate sales and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of RSAFS declines exceeding 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.3 percentage points, signals an overheating labor market that raises wage growth and input costs, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 100000 AND UNRATE monthly change < -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months with PAYEMS growth above 100,000 and UNRATE falling by more than 0.3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the year-over-year change in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and S&P 500 20-day forward returns; when GDPC1 grows by more than 2% YoY, the mechanism predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 2%.
